extracted.intended_audience: companies, in-house counsel, IP agents, accountants and advisers seeking Knowledge Development Box (KDB) tax relief in Ireland
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on what intellectual property and circumstances qualify for the Irish Knowledge Development Box (KDB) reduced corporation tax rate and how small-company secret inventions may be certified. Covers qualifying asset types, patent requirements, R&D nexus, and small company thresholds/certification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Qualifying intellectual property asset types
rubrics_metrics.description: The KDB provisions ... define qualifying intellectual property assets as: an invention protected by a qualifying patent; a computer program /copyrighted software, and inventions of small companies which are patentable but have not been patented and have been kept secret.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certain other IP such as supplementary protection certificates (SPCs) and plant breeders rights may also be qualifying assets. However, any marketing related IP such as trademarks, brands, image rights and other intellectual property used to market goods or services cannot be a qualifying asset. Short term patents are not qualifying assets. For more information consult the Revenue Guidance Notes at Revenue.ie.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement that qualifying assets result from R&D
rubrics_metrics.description: The qualifying assets must be the result of R&D.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: R&D is to be interpreted 'within the meaning of section 766 of the Taxes Consolidation Act 1997' — see Revenue Guidance for the applicable definition and tests for qualifying R&D activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Qualifying patent (general definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: A qualifying patent is defined as: '(a) a patent granted following substantive examination for novelty and inventive step, or (b) a patent, other than a short term patent within the meaning of section 63 of the Patents Act 1992, or an equivalent provision in another jurisdiction, where - (i) the Intellectual Property Office in the State, or equivalent Office elsewhere, has caused a search to be undertaken in relation to the invention and a search report (within the meaning of section 29 of the Patents Act 1992) prepared,……'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Short term patents are explicitly excluded. The majority of KDB claims are expected to relate to income from inventions protected by patents 'granted following substantive examination for novelty and inventive step.' Irish law (Patents Act 1992) has been amended to facilitate granting of long-term patents following substantive examination; Patents Rules were also amended (Patents (Amendment) Rules, 2017 S.I. No. 206 of 2017).

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusion of marketing-related IP
rubrics_metrics.description: Marketing related IP such as trademarks, brands, image rights and other intellectual property used to market goods or services cannot be a qualifying asset.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These categories are explicitly excluded from KDB eligibility even though they are IP — focus must be on IP that is the result of qualifying R&D and is of the types listed (patents, software, certain certified secret inventions, SPCs/plant breeder rights where applicable).

rubrics_metrics.name: Short-term patents are not qualifying
rubrics_metrics.description: Short term patents are not qualifying assets / patents for KDB purposes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page repeats that short term patents (within the meaning of section 63 of the Patents Act 1992) do not qualify; applicants should ensure the patent is a long-term patent or otherwise meets the qualifying-patent definition (substantive examination or an IPO search report).

rubrics_metrics.name: Small-company unpatented secret inventions eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Inventions of small companies which are patentable but have not been patented and have been kept secret may be eligible for KDB tax relief, provided they are so certified by the Controller of Intellectual Property.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To qualify under this route, the invention must share features of patents (i.e. be non-obvious, useful and novel) and the company must obtain certification from the Controller of Intellectual Property under the KDB Act (commenced 19 May 2017).

rubrics_metrics.name: Small company size and group thresholds for secret-invention route
rubrics_metrics.description: A small company is defined for KDB purposes as a company which has income arising from intellectual property of less than €7,500,000 in a 12 month accounting period, is a member of a group with group turnover of less than €50,000,000 and the company is a micro, small or medium sized company within the meaning of the Annex to Commission Recommendation 2003/361/EC of 6 May 2003.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only companies meeting all these numerical and SME-status criteria are eligible to use the 'patentable but kept secret' certification route; documentation and evidence supporting these thresholds will be required for certification and any KDB claim.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certification by the Controller of Intellectual Property required for certain assets
rubrics_metrics.description: The KDB Act empowers the Controller of Intellectual Property to provide the necessary certification (e.g., for small-company secret inventions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An application form for a KDB Certificate and guidance on the application process and procedure is available (link provided on the page). Applicants seeking KDB via the secret-invention route must apply to and obtain certification from the Controller before relying on that route.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tax relief mechanics and rate
rubrics_metrics.description: The KDB provides for a reduced rate of corporation tax (6.25% down from 12.5%) payable on such profits arising from qualifying IP assets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the financial effect of a successful KDB claim; applicants must ensure profits can be attributable to qualifying IP and calculated in accordance with Revenue guidance and TCA provisions to benefit from the reduced rate.
